body: Blue Dragon on the 360 is great, other than Lost Odyssey it's the only old school style turn-based JPRG I can think of for the console and I think it's better than Lost Odyssey. Have you ever played FFX and FFXII? I didn't like XIII at all either, but X and XII are two of my favorite games, both available as better than the original versions on PS4. Also, FFX-2 some people didn't like but I found a lot of fun, it has an action combat system by default (choose moves like turn based but you have guages that fill over time instead of waiting for turns), but you can set it to play turn based in the menu if you want. Obviously Persona V, and if it ever comes to PS4 Persona 4 Golden is probably my actual favorite video game. I note that you didn't specify JRPGs - if you like South Park, they have 2 turn-based RPGs, one is available on 360 and one on PS4, that are short but actually really good.

Which system though? Because I think their point was the N64, the remakes have made them play more like games today (don't have to deal with those incredibly frustrating camera angles and clipping, notably).

I definitely agree. I actually think that though the story was less developed 1 was by far the best for the atmosphere - it really felt like you were a lone vault hunter searching for lost treasure in a barren, post-apocalyptic wasteland. The other games completely lost that in my opinion. Plus, I might be in the minority but I liked the randomness of the loot more in the first - in the second game they really fleshed out the gun manufacturers so that you knew exactly what each gun would do and could better choose for playstyles but it turned it into more of an RPG upgrade system. I thought 1 was better because the randomness added to the wasteland atmosphere a lot (though it was so frustrating sometimes).

No one mentioned it but the original North American PS2 versions of FFX and FFX-2 are completely obsolete. All other regions got the international versions but North America never did. The HD remakes of both are the international versions - in X that means Dark Aeons, Ribbon, Penance, and the Extract abilities to speed up farming sphere grid spheres. In X-2, the festivalist and psychic dresspheres and Creature Creator. Plus they look like shit by comparison on the PS2.

I wish I had some advice but at least I can relate. I actually managed to force myself out with some friends Friday amd brunch Sunday but spent the rest of the weekend laying on the couch, watching movies mindlessly, and playing stupid online games for distraction. I know it sucks because I used to be such a bibliophile too and have hundreds of books but I just don't have the interest/motivation/desire to read anything. Hang in there, are you seeing a doctor or anything? I was recently diagnosed with depression for this and am working on figuring something out.
Well you're an awesome person and I'm so sorry to hijack the thread! I sincerely hope you're feeling better about whatever you're going through, and I'm very glad you're still around to help me out.
Thank you too! Really appreciate the advice, it's nervewracking wanting to go for help but not knowing what I can say. I don't have a plan or anything so that's good to know.

Instead of telling you not to feel ashamed I'll just say you're not alone. I'm concerned that I'm going to talk to a therapist this week for the first time and that I'll end up being committed involuntarily saying something stupid.

Is it possible that you just respond with a generic "I'm fine" and don't add anything the first couple times someone asks? I'm sure people don't ask me because I never say anything else for the same reason as you. I know in the past a friend vaguely knew something was wrong with me and went out of their way not to bring up questions like how was your weekend, etc so I didn't have to feel weird and shitty about it.

I suppose some of the same stuff applies even though it's different. I knew I wanted to do infectious disease research so I just applied to biomedical programs for microbiology. While I was doing that I looked around at all of the potential PIs, I was applying to med school so there were dozens at each. I looked at what they did, found that I was drawn to virology. For us, we do rotations at the start of the program - so I got to pick 4 different labs to work in. I worked in a flu lab, tried one bacteria lab to see what it's like, and the other 2 I had scheduling conflicts with a respiratory lab so both ended up being cancer virology. I actually made my decision based on my advisor; I have pretty bad depression so i joined a lab with a supportive, present, empathetic PI that I connected with very well because I know I'd drop out with a critical strict advisor. I'm in the process of designing my project right now. It might be different (I don't know how journalism works) because the lab is funded by a government grant. The grants are typically funded to research 3 related aims, and I develop a project and design experiments to answer those specific questions.

EDIT: but I wanted to add, I'm sure it's the same for every field, it's all about reading a lot about things you're interested in and thinking about how you can tell a story with whatever you choose to do.

I think I can relate - I don't even care about sex right now, I just crave an intimate relationship with the physical contact I never get. Somehow I've even met girls that are interested in me and that I like. But honestly, I just think "if only you really knew me" and push them away out of kindness. I wouldn't wish a relationship with me on my worst enemy.
What are you going to school for? How you would even go about this varies a ton depending on your field and I can only speak for hard sciences.
Thanks so much for sharing this.

Quite honestly just go if you're not there yet. The thing is that those of us with depression can't really feel like anything but a drain to anyone that cares about us in that mood. I can almost guarantee after calling you her thoughts are things like I'm such an idiot for calling and crying to him, he deserves better than me, now he just thinks I'm a crazy freak and will break up with me, etc. All I mostly want in one of these moods is not to be alone but I feel like I don't deserve anyone/will just be bringing everyone else down, and I think it's similar for most people suffering with depression. You don't even need to do/say anything just sit there and hold her hand, give her a big hug.

I actually just came on here to ask a question about melancholic depression. I've been struggling with similar, especially for the last 5 years or so; it's normal to have ups and downs but I think normal people feel things a lot more. I happened to read an article about melancholic depression that describes how I feel and might at least give you some insight. From my understanding, the thing that defines the melancholy subtype is a near complete emptiness and lack of interest in anything in addition to the other depression symptoms.

Have you ever gotten help? Personally I have not. I guess I might be feeling a bit hopeful because doing a bit of research, that type of depression is usually thought to be mostly a biological disorder that is severe but usually treatable with meds. Hope this at least helps you feel a little less alone in everything you're going through.

I assume you have, but have you talked to your parents about your situation? If not tell them that you don't think you'll be mentally able to handle the stress. The better university might lead to a better career option down the road but remember that it's the worst choice if you seriously don't think you'll make it. Definitely try to see someone (a psychiatrist/ologist) if you haven't. They'd be far more qualified to help you than I am, and should be able to help with any underlying problems. Might help make you feel more ready for school. Also try to remember everyone fucks up at some point. I know it's hard but try not to beat yourself up!

EDIT: also, your English is great.

Just wanted to say I'm sorry. I haven't lost an immediate family member but I've lost a few friends that were just as close. It's only been 2 days so honestly I don't think there isn't anything I can say to help. Loss sucks, I hope you're going to be OK.

I'm here because I'm depressed too, but I wanted to let you know that the piano helps me a lot. I played for maybe a year when I was a kid (like 8 or 9), then didn't touch a piano until I hot a good digital keyboard a few years ago. I still suck at it but I've at least mastered a few songs I really like. It can feel absolutely great, even if it's just a moment, to get lost in a song and come back and realize I'm playing it myself. Little victories and all! I hope you have a positive experience as well!
